title: ChatGPT can now read, draft, and send Apple Messages on Mac
subtitle: A new plugin gives the ChatGPT macOS app access to iMessage, SMS, and RCS conversations — with a Full Disk Access permission the archive it summarizes has never faced before.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI released a Messages plugin for the ChatGPT macOS app on August 20 that lets the assistant read, search, summarize, draft, and send messages across iMessage, SMS, and RCS conversations. The plugin is available on every ChatGPT tier including the free plan, works inside ChatGPT Work and Codex modes, and runs only on Apple Silicon Macs. Enabling it requires the user to grant Full Disk Access along with permissions for contact names and macOS automation. Sending a message requires per-action user approval by default, and OpenAI explicitly warns against granting persistent approval.

The permission set is the story. Full Disk Access lets the plugin see the local Messages database — years of conversations across every contact, not just the current chat. OpenAI acknowledges this in the launch documentation and pitches summarization of the archive as a feature: the plugin will tell you who you talk to most and what about. That is a different capability from drafting a single reply, and a considerably more revealing one. Whatever the model summarizes moves through OpenAI's servers under the standard API data-handling rules.

The launch fits a broader agentic push in 2026 — ChatGPT Work, Codex, Anthropic's Claude Cowork, Meta's Muse Spark screen context — all of which pull the assistant closer to the user's local data. The frontier of usefulness now runs through personal archives that used to be off-limits to any web service. The pattern will keep repeating: mail, calendar, notes, browser history, camera roll. Each one is a per-user consent decision that has to be made without a strong regulatory frame yet in place.

For learners: if you install this, treat every prompt to grant persistent approval as sending your archive to a third party. Read what Full Disk Access actually covers before you click through. The per-action confirmation is not a nag — it is the setting the vendor itself is telling you to keep on.
